messages.author: bb6cce4079fc308e
messages.subject: stepwiseqtl error message
parts:
Hi all,

I am working on a 4-way cross. When I implemented multiple qtl model using stepwiseqtl, I got the following error:

 > stepwiseqtl(t2.sim,max.qtl=5,method="hk",pheno.col = 1,verbose =
T,covar = NULL,penalties = penal)

  -Initial scan
Error in checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar, perm.strata,  :
   Number of rows in additive covariates is incorrect

I have also checked the cross by running checkcovar, where I specified  addcovar and intcovar as NULL. It looked fine.  It seems the error message was due to X chromosome.  Should I include sex as an additive co-variate?

I would really appreciate it if someone has any idea.

Thanks!

Xiaodong

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] stepwiseqtl error message
parts:
We wrote stepwiseqtl() not thinking about a 4-way cross, and I think there are a number of places where it just won't work properly. For now, I think it's best to not use stepwiseqtl() for a 4-way cross at all.

Sorry,
karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] stepwiseqtl error message
parts:
Hi Karl,

Thank you for the info. I am trying to polish MQM manually. But I also got the error message by running addint as following:

> out.ai <-addint(t2.sim, qtl=qtl, formula=y~Q1+Q2+Q3)
Error in model.frame.default(formula = pheno ~ Xadjustment$sexpgmcovar,  : 
  variable lengths differ (found for 'Xadjustment$sexpgmcovar')
In addition: Warning message:
In addint(t2.sim, qtl = qtl, formula = y ~ Q1 + Q2 + Q3) :
  Dropping 4 individuals with missing phenotypes.

Is it due to the same reason as stepwiseqtl()? 

Thanks a lot!
